title: Augmented comparison of Cartan--Eilenberg bicomplexes
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and F:A→B an exact additive functor. Let K and L be Z-indexed cochain complexes, u:F(K)→L a chain map, and I,J bicomplexes with complex index Z and resolution index N [def-sp-double-complex-total], augmented from K[0] and L[0] in the resolution degree. Assume I and J vanish below respective common bounds in the complex degree. Assume their augmented object, cycle, boundary and homology columns are quasi-isomorphisms from the corresponding objects concentrated in resolution degree zero. Assume the object, cycle, boundary and homology terms of J are injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No injectivity assumption on I is imposed. Then there is a bicomplex morphism φ:F(I)→J satisfying, for every p, F(εIᵖ) followed by φᵖ,⁰ equals uᵖ followed by εJᵖ, with the degree-zero single objects identified by singleObjXSelf. No total-complex or filtration conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: Choose $i=\min(i_I,i_J)$. For $P(n)=i+n$, retain an augmented boundary map in degree $P(n)$ as the inductive state. At $n=0$ take the zero boundary map: the target original-object column in degree $i-1$ is zero, so its augmentation gives the required boundary equation.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ce-comparison-column-step] to the retained boundary map in degree $P(n)$. Obtain an augmented original-object comparison $x_n$ and an outgoing boundary comparison $b_{n+1}$, with both image inclusion/factorization squares. Package these together and recursively retain exactly that $b_{n+1}$ using Nat.rec. Thus the map used as outgoing boundary at stage $n$ is definitionally the incoming map at stage $n+1$. The local lemma uses just the stated resolution data in degrees $P(n)$ and $P(n)+1$.

Compose the outgoing factorThruImage square at stage $n$ with image.ι and substitute the incoming image.ι square at stage $n+1$. Functoriality of $G=F.mapHomologicalComplex$ and image.fac give $x_n d_J=G(d_I)x_{n+1}$. Remove the $P(n+1)-1=P(n)$ transports by equality elimination. Define all column maps below $i$ as zero; horizontal commutation there follows because the source column is zero, including the transition into degree $i$. Extend the chosen maps above $i$ to all integer indices using $(p-i).toNat$, and assemble them with HomologicalComplex.Hom. The original augmentation equations hold above $i$ by the local lemma and below $i$ because the target column is zero. This proves the unchanged displayed conclusion.
